subject: build R package from source old gcc inla.dynload.workaround() error

messages.author: 0965a429193e691b
messages.subject: build R package from source old gcc inla.dynload.workaround() error
parts:
Hello,
 
I'm hoping I could get some general advice for building INLA R package from source with old GLIBC (2.12) on a system where I do not have root permissions.

Through regular package install via:

install.packages("INLA", repos=c(getOption("repos"), 
        INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/testing"), dep=TRUE)

library(INLA)

## example
fake.locations = matrix(c(0,0,5,5, 0, 5, 5, 0), nrow = 4, byrow = T)
mesh.sim = inla.mesh.2d(loc = fake.locations, max.edge=c(1, 1))


I get the common message which I've seen posted about before (for example here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/r-inla-discussion-group/R2uLnUainWM)

My error message:

/mylibpath/rlibs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /mylibpath/rlibs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher)
/mylibpath/rlibs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /mylibpath/rlibs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libgsl.so.23)
Error in fmesher.read(prefix, "manifold") : 
  File '/tmp/RtmpCVHNmp/fmesher3f514160b593.manifold' does not exist.


I've tried the solution:

INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()
mesh.sim = inla.mesh.2d(loc = fake.locations, max.edge=c(1, 1))

and I receive the error:

FATAL: kernel too old
Error in fmesher.read(prefix, "manifold") : 
  File '/tmp/RtmpCVHNmp/fmesher3f51415d0b65.manifold' does not exist.

Is there any other available workarounds, or advice on how to build from source?

Thanks very much for any help or advice,
Dan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] build R package from source old gcc inla.dynload.workaround() error
parts:
Hi

there is a tar'ed build directory at

hrue.r-inla-download.org/my-laptop-O2.tgz

that you could use. you may not need all of it (like the gsl, etc),
but you just recompile, like 'make amd' and 'make inla' and 'make
fmesher' at the end.

doing

make update

will update the repo. Otherwise, you can set

export INLA_VERSION=Version_19.10.06

to compile that one (so its in correspondance with the R-package
itself)

set 'inla.call' and 'fmesher.call' to these new builds, and you'll be
fine.

H
